thread:
maria: Heads up — seeing a sustained +15% GPU Pending in us-west1b since the new rack came up. Tiny pods (request 0.25 GPU) are getting evicted/requeued a lot. Anyone else?

samir: yep, spike started ~08:18 UTC. saw a cluster of preempts and re-schedules. scheduler logs show a bunch of "FilterFailed: InsufficientGPUResource" churn, then preemption.

kevin: fwiw we added r-west1b-07 yesterday (label gpu=small) and the scheduler's affinity weighting still prefers nvlink racks. tiny pods prefer old racks -> fragmentation + orphaned slots.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu_fragmentation_rate(us-west1b) = 12.4% over 30m. evict_count(us-west1b) = 114 in 30m.

maria: quick mitigation idea: raise taint toleration TTL for tiny-pods so they stick to their current nodes for 2m, and try a packing-floor heuristic for small requests so scheduler avoids scattering fractional GPUs across racks. e.g. set packing-floor=0.5 for pods with request <0.5 GPU.

samir: ran a quick grep on scheduler: `kubectl logs -n kube-system scheduler-0 | grep fragment` -> sample: 
```
I0908 08:20:12.345678 1 scheduler.go:123] scoring node r-west1b-03 score=12 (fragment_penalty=8)
I0908 08:20:12.345700 1 scheduler.go:123] rejecting pod tiny-model-xyz: FilterFailed(InsufficientGPUResource)
```
Not great.

kevin: Packing-floor sounds reasonable as a canary. downside: might increase reserved capacity / wasted GPU legs. Ops calc: reserving to avoid churn could add ~8% util slack (but saves re-schedule overhead).

ops_lead: cost tradeoff: 8% warm slack vs ~20% extra scheduling + pod startup costs and potential SLA hits. I'm leaning to a 6h canary in us-west1b-c only, monitor frag_rate + evict_count + tail latency.

maria: plan: kevin, can you roll packing-floor=0.5 to canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC on us-west1b-c only? add telemetry tags: metric=frag_rate, evict_count, pack_floor_override. If regress, revert within 15m. @ops_lead ok? :thumbsup:

kevin: SG. I'll patch the scheduler configmap and attach a rollback job. config snippet I'll apply:
```
policy:
  packing:
    default_floor: 0.0
    overrides:
      tiny_pod: 0.5
```
Will also export current rack utilization before the run.

samir: +1. also will add a quick probe that simulates 200 tiny-pod starts to stress the path in canary and validate no NVLINK-affinity regressions.

ops_lead: agree. set canary window 6h, revert if evict_count increases or frag_rate > baseline by 5% after 30m. keep me posted.

maria: thanks. tagging infra oncall just in case.

samir: note: we should also check kubelet attach/detach latencies (seen small bump) — might amplify churn. i'll add attach_latency metric. :mag_right:
